- When sentiment is consistently negative or neutral over recent days, model tends to over-forecast upward; correct by reducing forecast slope or adding downward bias.
- After sharp spikes in price (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply lagged mean reversion or cap forecast at 1.5x recent peak.
- In high bearish event balance (bearish > bullish), model under-responds to downward pressure — adjust forecast downward by 5–10% of recent mean or add -0.2 to -0.5 to sentiment-weighted drift.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 or low positive values, model tends to flatline — introduce slight downward drift or use moving average of 3–5 prior days to anchor forecast.
- In high auction supply events (supply_net negative), model often fails to anticipate sharp drops — add 0.5–1.0 to forecast adjustment if supply_net > -10.00.
- When bullish events dominate (bullish > bearish), model may over-forecast — reduce forecast by 2–5% of recent mean if bullish > 15.00.
- Forecast should not exceed 1.2x the 30-day moving average unless accompanied by strong bullish sentiment or recent auction spikes.
